The search · Google Maps, 12 November 2026

Montagu's guest houses are on the list. Glen Eden isn't.

We searched "guest houses in Montagu" on Google Maps. After two paid ads, Google lists about thirty places to stay. Glen Eden Farm is not one of them.

Being 14 km out on Route 62 is part of it. The bigger part is on the next slide: your reviews are split across three separate listings, so none of them looks as strong as the farm really is.

The problem · one farm, three listings

291 reviews, split three ways.

Search "Glen Eden Farm" and Google shows three separate pins: the farm, Entrance 1 and Entrance 2. Each one carries part of your reviews. Together they hold 291, three times as many as In Abundance, the first guest house on the Montagu list.

Nothing is wrong with the stay. Your happy guests are simply spread across three places. From day one, every review request we send points to one listing, so the count builds where travellers look.

The website · Google search, 12 November 2026

Found for the small searches. Missing from the big one.

Your website already ranks first to third when someone searches for glamping or camping in Montagu. But "accommodation Montagu", searched 1,000 to 10,000 times a month, shows only booking sites and directories. Glen Eden isn't in the first 30 results.

How it works · when a stay wasn't perfect

An unhappy guest reaches you before they reach Google.

A guest who rates their stay 3 or lower gets a private message asking what went wrong. You hear about it straight away, and can put it right while it's still fresh.

Every guest is still sent the Google link, because Google doesn't allow review invitations to go only to happy guests. What changes is that you hear about the problem first, privately, and get the chance to fix it.

Guests' names are blurred to protect their privacy.

WhatsApp · TO Strand, Port Edward
How it works · already running at Dot Com Restaurant

Answered in a minute. Handed to you when it matters.

A guest asks a simple question on WhatsApp and gets the answer straight away. When they ask for something only a person can decide, it is handed over, and the guest is told when to expect a reply.

At Glen Eden, you're out at the touch farm or behind the bar at Beaney Peanut when someone asks which cottage takes the dog, whether the camp sites have power, or how far you are from Montagu. They get the answer in a minute, and every booking comes to you. You can step into any chat yourself, whenever you want to.

How the first month runs

Reviews live in week one. Your new website within the month.

Day 1

Kickoff

An hour together. You give us access to Google, WhatsApp and your booking system, and tell us how the farm likes to sound.

Week 1

Asked and answered

Review requests switched on after every checkout, all pointing to one listing, and the WhatsApp assistant answering guests, evenings included.

Week 2

Every Google review replied

Google replies running in your voice, and your changes to the new website made.

Weeks 3 to 4

Tuned and live

The assistant's answers checked against real guest questions, the new website moved onto glenedenfarm.co.za once you've approved it, and a half-hour call to walk you through everything.

Fair questions

You stay in control of your farm.

Your voice
A bot talking to my guests?

It only answers facts you've approved: cottages, glamping, camping, pets, activities, directions. Bookings, special requests and complaints always come to you. If you'd like to see Google replies before they go out, we send them to you to approve first.

Your guests
What about their details?

Guest details are used only to send your review request after checkout. They are never shared, sold or used for anything else, and they stay with the farm.

Your call
What if it doesn't work for us?

Month to month, 30 days' notice, no long contract. Everything we set up stays yours. And since every guest still gets the Google link, nothing about your reviews is ever filtered.
